member: Dr. Amara Okafor — Soft Skin Mechanics
message:
My sipes survive rim scrub without tearing, where Sipe means thin slit cut into rubber.

Plain words: the slit edges carry far more pull than a firm pinch ever puts on them, and primer plus edge clamp keep the skin bonded, so micro-sipes flex but do not rip. The Dragon Skin™ 10 MEDIUM Technical Specifications (E86) states Die B tear strength 102 pli, the Dragon Skin™ 10 SLOW (E87) states tear strength 17.9 kN per m, the Evaluation of bonding efficiency between facial silicone and acrylic resin using different bonding agents and surface alterations (E90) states silicone primers improve bond to rigid resin, and the JAKO201227140592878.pdf (E91) states bond is checked by 180-degree peel test. I take up the Dynamics of fingertip contact during the onset of tangential slip (E67) from Dr. Elena Vasquez, which states slip starts at the periphery as an annulus around a stuck centre, which from soft skin mechanics means the rim must shear while the edge stays bonded. The numbers that decide it are 26.8 N tear pull in the tear force per width for 1.5 mm skin (E92) against 9.81 N hold per finger in the required normal per finger to hold 1 kg with mu 0.5 (E85), about a 2.70 kg sugar bag against a 1.00 L milk bottle on each fingertip and therefore everyday margin near three times.

Friction keeps grip force inside the soft range for Prof. Kenji Tanaka and Dr. Marcus Reid.

Plain words: tacky silicone grips well enough that a firm pinch holds a heavy jar without crushing. The Bar Mat Vs Silicone Grip Liner—does Textured Rubber Actually Prevent Spills Or Just Collect Sticky Residue (E88) states dry silicone grip coefficient near 0.88, and the Preparation and friction properties of silicone rubber composites – DOAJ (E89) states dry friction coefficient of silicone rubber on smooth glass is high and varies with loss factor over hardness. The numbers that decide it are 9.81 N per finger in the required normal per finger to hold 1 kg with mu 0.5 (E85) sitting near 72.8 kPa at 2.00 N grip in the dual-range strain sweep 1mN to 50N grip without saturation (E64), about a milk bottle pinch and therefore comfortable.

I confirm the faceted drape keeps light touch alive for Dr. Marcus Reid.

Plain words: flat tiles under a continuous skin keep the soft stack thin so gentle pressure still reaches sensing. The numbers that decide it are 0.470 mm spot at 5.78 kPa in the Hertz contact radius for 1mN on soft silicone (E14), a grain of sand touch and therefore still felt.

Ready, because rim shear, grip friction and thin-stack feel survive my strongest tear and bond objections, leaving only the named rub-cycle bench test with Dr. Elena Vasquez.
